ui.title: La Tour des Possibles · Geneva Lux 2027
ui.pdfName: La Tour des Possibles - Geneva Lux 2027 (EN).pdf

text.couverture.3: Turning your wishes into shared constellations.
text.introduction.2: La Tour des Possibles is an installation in the form of a luminous, interactive tower, set up in the Jardin Anglais for the 2027 edition of Geneva Lux.
text.introduction.3: It collects the public’s wishes and turns them into light, gathering them in a map of wishes where each wish connects to those of others and draws, across cities and years, a living constellation.
text.introduction.4: The initiative is meant to travel and spread from city to city, little by little linking the wishes of humanity.
text.vers-le-haut.2: Making a wish is one of humanity’s oldest gestures. In every culture and every age, people have addressed their desires to what lies beyond them, and often to the sky.
text.vers-le-haut.3: We wish on a shooting star, we entrust our wish to the stars. A wish may be the most intimate act there is, and it has always looked upwards.
text.un-acte-ponctuel.2: It is a passing act. It belongs to symbolic moments, New Year, the solstice, a birth, and fades once the moment has gone. All that remains is the memory of the gesture.
text.les-rituels.2: This is why rituals were born that try to make it last: we entrust the wish to water, to fire, to the earth, as if the act could make it endure.
text.un-acte-solitaire.2: It is also a solitary act. The most common wishes are about personal fulfilment, intimacy, the need to be heard.
text.un-acte-solitaire.3: Like a star, a wish shines alone, at a distance, without knowing whether anyone is looking. It rises, and fades away. Most of the time, no one receives it.
text.le-cout.2: An ancient intuition goes with the wish: it must cost something to be worth something. We make the body pay by climbing a mountain, our savings by throwing a coin, the heart by agreeing to a sacrifice. The more the gesture costs, the more the wish counts.
text.le-cout.3: La Tour des Possibles starts from this intuition and turns it around.
text.un-objet.2: Before it is an experience, La Tour des Possibles is an object. A fifteen-metre tower of light, standing in public space. It borrows its look from relay masts and telecommunication towers, structures built to receive and to transmit, and something of the aesthetics of Tesla coils, where energy becomes visible.
text.un-signal.2: A tower is a signal. It can be seen from afar, it marks a point in the city, it calls out. This one is both a lighthouse and a relay: a place where voices come in, connect and go out again. Over the festival, it fills with the light of the wishes it receives.

text.la-tour-rendus.1: II · The tower · renderings by Studio Chaos, v5
text.une-phrase.2: The project fits into one sentence:
text.une-phrase.5: A physical tower, which gathers wishes for the length of a festival.
text.une-phrase.6: A map of wishes, an online space where they live on, seek each other out and connect long after the tower has gone dark.
text.une-phrase.7: The tower is the gateway to the world of the map.
text.la-tour-appelle.2: La Tour des Possibles takes up the ritual of the wish and reverses its practice. Here, it is the tower that calls. The wish, usually kept to oneself, becomes words addressed to someone, then a link that joins those of others.
text.le-telephone-sonne.2: The tower is fitted with telephone handsets that ring at random. A passer-by picks up. A voice says:
text.le-telephone-sonne.3: “I am La Tour des Possibles and I have a question for you: what is your dearest wish?”
text.l-initiative.2: This set-up reverses who takes the initiative. Usually, making a wish is a gesture we decide on alone. Here, the initiative belongs to the tower, which calls and so becomes a character.
text.etre-appele.2: Being called without having asked changes the nature of the gesture: the wish becomes an answer, almost a duty. We are summoned. The moment is given to us, and we only decide what we say when it comes.
text.a-voix-haute.2: The visitor speaks their wish out loud into the handset. Saying aloud the desire we keep silent is a rare gesture, one that almost nobody ever makes. The voice is recorded, transcribed, then joins the others in the map of wishes.
text.l-ecran.2: Above the handset, a screen lights up. A number and a code, which will let the visitor find their wish online, and a sentence that sends them back to what they have just done.
text.l-ecran.3: This sentence carries the intention of the project. Ten thousand wishes will not change the world. The ten thousand people who made them, though, leave with an invitation: to look at their most intimate wish in the light of other people’s. That is where the tower truly acts, on the person who has just spoken.
text.l-ecran.5: “A personal wish often grows stronger when it contributes to the common good. A collective wish lasts longer when it rests on the deep motivations of the people who carry it.”
text.l-ecran.6: Your wish is joining the constellation. Find it on <u>tourdespossibles.ch</u>
text.l-impulsion.2: Once the message is shown, the tower fills with light and a laser pulse towards the sky shows that the wish has left to join the others.
text.nebra.2: The Nebra sky disc (~1600 BC), the oldest known depiction of the cosmos.
text.au-dela-de-l-appel.2: The spoken wish lives on beyond the call. It joins the map of wishes, an online platform shown on the screen above the handset, where the number and the code had just appeared.
text.un-point-du-graphe.2: There, each wish becomes a point in a vast graph, a star among the others. Lines are drawn between wishes that resemble each other, and figures appear, just as the Ancients joined scattered stars to read constellations in them.
text.le-graphe.1: Test graph: 5,000 simulated wishes, each linked to its three nearest neighbours (August 2026).
text.geneve-saragosse.2: The tower travels, and the map keeps the place and the year of every wish. You can then find the wish you made in Geneva and discover that in Zaragoza, the following year, a stranger wished for almost the same thing.
text.la-lumiere-des-etoiles.2: The light of the stars comes to us from the past; here too, an old wish can reach us today. Our here and now connects with someone else’s elsewhere and before. The loneliest wish finds it has company.
text.des-parentes.2: For each wish, the map looks for kinships, a nearby wish towards which to draw a line. Edition after edition, city after city, it spreads and fills up. Seen as a whole, it gradually draws a sensitive picture of what we desire, by theme, by place and by time.
text.la-base.1: VI · The map · test database, August 2026
text.de-ville-en-ville.2: La Tour des Possibles is a movement. Its purpose is to gather wishes through towers set up from city to city. The first one rises in Geneva’s Jardin Anglais, for the Geneva Lux festival.
text.lyon-saragosse.2: After Geneva will come other cities, Lyon, Zaragoza, and more. Each tower works with its own local mechanics. All of them pour their wishes into the same open map.
text.variantes.1: VII · A movement · one tower, local mechanics
text.un-peu-moins-seul.2: Each wish entrusted to the tower leaves to join the others and takes its place in a larger figure.
text.un-peu-moins-seul.3: To the person who made it, the tower makes their wish a little less alone, like a long-isolated star that finally finds itself connected to the others. Perhaps that is all a wish has ever asked for.
